column4: 送 in the "see off" sense means to walk/ride with someone as they leave; bare "despedir" reads first as "to fire (an employee)" to a Spanish speaker, which is the wrong picture entirely

希望 is "to hope", but "esperar" is already used for 等 (h1 w020, "to wait"); esperar alone is genuinely ambiguous between "wait" and "hope" in Spanish, so keeping both words on "esperar" doubles that confusion — desear keeps 希望 unambiguous
一下 softens a verb into "do it briefly/a bit" (等一下 = wait a moment); "una vez" reads as counting occurrences ("once"), which is really 一次's job, not 一下's
鱼 covers both the living animal and the food, same as English "fish"; "pescado" alone only covers the food sense (a live fish in a story or pond is a "pez", not a "pescado")
早上 means "morning"; plain "mañana" collides with 明天 ("tomorrow" = mañana). The noun with the article marks it as "the morning", not the adverb "tomorrow"
最 is the superlative marker ("the most/-est", e.g. 最好 = the best), not the comparative "more"; bare "más" reads as comparative and loses that distinction
